# dlas2

> Computes the singular values of a 2-by-2 triangular matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlas2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlas2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlas2( f, g, h, ssmin, ssmax ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `f` | `number` | The (1,1) element |
| `g` | `number` | The (1,2) element |
| `h` | `number` | The (2,2) element |
| `ssmin` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the smaller singular value |
| `ssmax` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the larger singular value |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `f`: The (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `g`: The (1,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `h`: The (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `ssmin`: The smaller singular value.
- `ssmax`: The larger singular value.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlas2.strided( f, g, h, ssmin, ssmax ) → void
```

Computes singular values of a 2-by-2 triangular matrix, using alternative indexing semantics.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `f` | `number` | The (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `g` | `number` | The (1,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `h` | `number` | The (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix |
| `ssmin` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the smaller singular value |
| `ssmax` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the larger singular value |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `f`: The (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `g`: The (1,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `h`: The (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `ssmin`: The smaller singular value.
- `ssmax`: The larger singular value.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlas2()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAS2`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlas2.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import dlas2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlas2';

// Using the standard interface:
const ssmin = new Float64Array( 1 );
const ssmax = new Float64Array( 1 );

dlas2( 1, 1, 1, ssmin, ssmax );
let out = new Float64Array( [ ssmin[ 0 ], ssmax[ 0 ] ] );
console.log( out );

// Using the strided interface:
dlas2.strided( 1, 1, 1, ssmin, ssmax );
out = new Float64Array( [ ssmin[ 0 ], ssmax[ 0 ] ] );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAS2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLAS2 computes the singular values of the 2-by-2 matrix

$$
\begin{bmatrix} F & G \\ 0 & H \end{bmatrix}
$$

On return, `SSMIN` is the smaller singular value and `SSMAX` is the larger singular value.

### Further Details

Barring over/underflow, all output quantities are correct to within a few units in the last place (ulps), even in the absence of a guard digit in addition/subtraction.

In IEEE arithmetic, the code works correctly if one matrix element is infinite.

Overflow will not occur unless the largest singular value itself overflows, or is within a few ulps of overflow.

Underflow is harmless if underflow is gradual. Otherwise, results may correspond to a matrix modified by perturbations of size near the underflow threshold.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
